newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest hog runs seen light again Friday -trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest hog runs seen light again Friday -trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog markets Friday were expected to be hit again by howling winds, blowing snow and dangerously cold wind chills overnight which likely will again stall hog movement, livestock dealers said.
The tighter hog marketings Friday were expected to result in packers paying steady to $0.50 higher prices compared with Thursday's top values.
Top prices for hogs delivered to plants in Iowa and southern Minnesota could range from $54.50 to $55.50 per cwt, they said.
Southern Minnesota buyers said major roads were reopened near midday Thursday, allowing producers to move enough hogs for at least one plant to operate full shifts on Friday.

Several major packers reported delays Thursday at plants in South Dakota, southern Minnesota, Iowa, Illinois and Indiana. Illinois hog buyers said weather-tightened marketings boosted hog prices as high as $57.00 on hogs delivered to the plant, with most hogs going for $53.00 to $55.00.
Not many hogs traded. About 700 hogs moved through buying stations that can move 8,000 on a good day, one central Illinois dealer said.
Some buyers did not make it to buying stations due to snow and ice, the dealer said.
Indiana/Ohio hog prices were seen steady-higher, with top prices at the plant ranging $53.50 to $54.50.

USDA estimated Thursday slaughter at 251,000 hogs, compared with 325,000 a week ago and 288,000 a year ago. Week to date slaughter was estimated at 1.302 million head, compared with 1.355 million a week ago and year ago.
